english.title: Bring / throw / otherwise convey a thing into a prison to facilitate escape - Prison Act 1952
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), intending to facilitate the escape of **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), a prisoner, brought, threw or otherwise conveyed **(..SPECIFY THE ARTICLE..) into

(A)_[His Majesty's prison at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..)]_
(B)_[His Majesty's remand centre at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), being an institution to which section 43 of the Prison Act 1952 applied]_
(C)_[His Majesty's young offender institution at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), being an institution to which section 43 of the Prison Act 1952 applied]_
(D)_[His Majesty's secure training centre at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), being an institution to which section 43 of the Prison Act 1952 applied]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 39(1)(b)(i) and (2) of the Prison Act 1952.

english.notes:
(i) This offence was substituted in section 39 of the Prison Act 1952 by section 21 of the Offender Management Act 2007 with effect from 1st April 2008.
(ii) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.
